jobs.title: Senior Technical Project Manager – Chlorinated Solvent Remediation
jobs.description:
Are you driven to grow, lead, and make a meaningful impact? At Apex, we’re building more than a consulting and engineering firm—we’re creating a place where your career accelerates, your contributions matter, and your potential is fully realized. We believe your growth is our growth, which is why we invest in your development at every stage of your career. Here, you’ll work on projects that shape communities, protect the environment, and create lasting impact, all while being empowered with the autonomy and flexibility to do your best work.

Fueled by high-quality delivery, exceptional client retention, and strategic acquisitions, Apex Companies continues to rank among the fastest-growing firms in the AEC industry, recently recognized by the Zweig Group for our industry-leading growth. Our success is grounded in strong leadership, a collaborative culture, and a shared commitment to delivering exceptional outcomes.

As we continue to expand, we're looking for high-performing professionals who are ready to lead, collaborate, innovate, and create impact. At Apex, you help shape what's next. When we succeed together, we share in that success. All Apex positions are eligible for annual bonus opportunities, reinforcing our commitment to recognizing and rewarding meaningful contributions that drive our collective growth.

The Senior Technical Project Manager (PM) will lead and manage complex environmental investigation, remediation, and compliance projects involving chlorinated solvent impacts in soil, groundwater, sediment, soil vapor, and indoor air. The role requires strong technical leadership, client management, project delivery, staff development, and business development capabilities. Experience with large industrial, aerospace, manufacturing, military, and brownfield remediation programs is highly desirable.

Key Responsibilities

Project and Program Management

Manage large-scale environmental remediation projects from proposal through closure.
Develop project scopes, schedules, budgets, and health and safety plans.
Lead multidisciplinary teams of geologists, engineers, hydrogeologists, risk assessors, and environmental scientists.
Monitor project financial performance, including revenue, profitability, utilization, and forecasting.
Coordinate subcontractors, laboratories, drilling contractors, and remediation vendors.
Maintain quality assurance and quality control standards.

Technical Leadership

Serve as a technical lead for sites impacted by:
PCE (Tetrachloroethylene)
TCE (Trichloroethylene)
cis-1,2-DCE
Vinyl Chloride
Other chlorinated VOCs

Design and oversee:
Site investigations
Groundwater characterization
Soil vapor intrusion assessments
Human health and ecological risk assessments
Remedial investigations/feasibility studies (RI/FS)
Corrective action programs

Evaluate and implement remediation technologies such as:
In situ chemical reduction (ISCR)
In situ chemical oxidation (ISCO)
Enhanced reductive dechlorination (ERD)
Thermal remediation
Soil vapor extraction (SVE)
Dual-phase extraction (DPE)
Air sparging
Monitored natural attenuation (MNA)

Client Relationship Management

Act as primary client contact for key accounts.
Support strategic planning with industrial, aerospace, petroleum, manufacturing, and government clients.
Prepare and present technical findings to clients, regulators, and stakeholders.
Maintain long-term client relationships while identifying opportunities for additional services.

Business Development

Lead proposal preparation and pricing.
Support capture planning and opportunity pursuit.
Identify new clients and expand existing accounts.
Participate in industry organizations and conferences.

Regulatory Expertise

Demonstrated Experience Working With

EPA CERCLA/Superfund programs
RCRA Corrective Action
State cleanup programs
Vapor intrusion guidance
UST and industrial facility closure programs
California DTSC and Regional Water Board programs

Qualifications

BS in Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering, Geological Engineering, Hydrogeology, Geology, or related field.
12+ years of environmental consulting experience.
7+ years managing complex remediation projects.
Demonstrated success managing projects exceeding $500K to $5M+ annually.
Significant chlorinated solvent investigation and remediation experience.
California PE, PG, CHG, PMP, REM, CHMM (preferred)

Why You'll Love Working For Us

Company-subsidized medical and dental.
Company-paid life, short, and long-term disability.
401k match, tuition assistance, and more.
Cross-training and the ability to work on a variety of projects.
Performance-based bonuses or other incentives.
Working with the best and brightest in the industry.
2,000+ employee national firm with 70+ locations across the US.

jobs.title: Environmental Health Officer
jobs.description:
Protect public health. Make a difference in your community.

Help protect and promote community health as an Environmental Health Officer with Metro South Health, investigating public health matters and delivering essential environmental health services.

Your New Role

Join Metro South Health as an Environmental Health Officer and help protect public health across our community through environmental health regulation, investigation and evidence-based practice.

Deliver environmental health services, investigate public health matters and administer Queensland public health legislation.
Engage with industry, community members and external agencies regarding public health regulation and communicable diseases.
Work collaboratively within an interprofessional Public Health Unit, contributing specialist expertise, education and support to staff and students.
Contribute to quality improvement, research and service development initiatives that strengthen environmental health outcomes.

About you:

You are a motivated and collaborative professional with strong communication skills and a commitment to protecting and promoting public health.

Demonstrate the ability to deliver high-quality, evidence-based environmental health services and enforce public health legislation.
Communicate effectively and work collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams, stakeholders and members of the public.
Demonstrate a commitment to ongoing professional development, continuous learning and the education of students.
Bring initiative and a willingness to contribute to service improvement, research and the development of environmental health practices.

Check out our quick tips and application essentials!

What We Can Offer You

We offer a family-friendly work environment that supports you in making the most of Queensland's laid-back lifestyle.
We are renowned for teaching and research excellence with strong relations with Queensland's leading tertiary institutions.
We want to empower you to build a long-term career, with countless opportunities to learn and grow, no matter your role
You'll have all the benefits of working for Queensland's world-class public health system including generous leave entitlements, attractive salary and remuneration packages, salary packaging and access to relevant professional development allowances and/or leave, study and research assistance, corporate discounts and employee wellness programs.

About us:

Role

Metro South Public Health Unit's primary role is to enhance the health of the community by preventing disease, illness and injury, promoting and protecting health and wellbeing, and managing risk. This is achieved through:

Enhanced health surveillance
Management of environmental hazards, food safety and standards
Communicable disease control and immunisations
Public health incident management
Medical entomology
Health promotion

INTEGRITY | COMPASSION | ACCOUNTABILITY | RESPECT | ENGAGEMENT | EXCELLENCE

Our values were created by employees for employees to shape our culture and inspire positive interactions in the workplace. Diversity of ideas, skills, traditions, and customs is celebrated as one of our greatest strengths. Having a workforce that reflects and understands the needs and expectations of our community is important to delivering safe, kinder, and more inclusive care.

We recognise our strength comes from the diversity of our people and so we encourage people of all genders, ethnicities, ages, abilities, languages, sexual orientation, and family responsibilities to apply.

We are better together .

jobs.title: Water Resources Sector Manager - VIC
jobs.description:
Company Description

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM’s Water Resources business is seeking an engaging and collaborative Sector Manager for our Victoria team.

Our Water Resources team delivers integrated, multidisciplinary services from flood risk and hydraulic modelling to drainage design, water quality and nature based solutions, across a range of projects including infrastructure, energy, defence, water utilities and airports.

This key leadership role will give you the opportunity to build networks across AECOM in Australia, New Zealand, and globally, from business operations through to management, while working closely with our leading specialists. Elevate your professional profile and carve a career pathway that truly makes a difference.

How you’ll make a difference

Guide the growth of the VIC Water Resources sector by fostering strong client partnerships, expanding market presence, diversifying our portfolio of services, and successfully delivering projects across the region.
Ensure technical and delivery excellence while maintaining the highest standards of quality, safety, governance, and client satisfaction.
Cultivate a collaborative, high-performing team culture by mentoring staff, providing technical direction, and nurturing growth.
Leverage regional and global expertise to drive innovation, implement best practices, and enhance delivery outcomes.

Qualifications

The following qualifications and experience are highly desired, but if you don’t tick all the boxes, you could still be a perfect fit for this role. Please apply, all applications will be considered.

The qualities that help you thrive

A relevant tertiary degree, CPEng, and ideally 20+ years of experience in water resources, including drainage, flooding, nature based solutions, water balance and yield assessments, and integrated water management.
A proactive, problem-solving mindset with the ability to champion innovative ideas, encourage initiative, and apply creative solutions.
A passion for leadership, mentoring, collaboration, and building strong relationships across diverse stakeholders.
Commercial and strategic acumen, with the ability to make informed decisions that balance profitability, efficiency, and market insight.

Additional Information

Why you’ll love working with us

Flexible work arrangements, including alternative start/finish times, part-time, job-sharing and hybrid work options
Purchase up to 6 weeks additional annual leave per year
Volunteer and representation leave
Flex public holidays – swap Easter or other holidays for ones that suit you better

Ready to push the limits of what’s possible?

We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, including those with disabilities, additional health or mental health needs, and/or neurodiverse conditions. If you require any adjustments during the hiring process, please let us know.

Applications are reviewed as they come in, and the role may close earlier than expected, so if this opportunity sounds like you, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

Learn more about life at AECOM:
LinkedIn, Facebook , Instagram, X, YouTube - explore our AECOM voices, employee stories, latest projects, and much more!

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

AECOM acknowledges the Traditional Owners and Custodians of the lands on which we, our clients and our communities live and work around Australia. We pay our respects to their cultures and to their Elders — past, present, and emerging. We are committed to connecting to Country in our work through meaningful engagement with First Nations peoples and businesses. Find out more about our Australian Reconciliation Action Plan here: https://aecom.com/au/our-vision-for-reconciliation/.

About AECOM

AECOM is the world’s trusted infrastructure consulting firm, delivering professional services throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. On projects spanning transportation, buildings, water, new energy and the environment, our public- and private-sector clients trust us to solve their most complex challenges. Our teams are driven by a common purpose to deliver a better world through our unrivaled technical and digital expertise, a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion, and a commitment to environmental, social and governance priorities. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm and its Professional Services business had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. See how we are delivering sustainable legacies for generations to come at aecom.com and @AECOM.

Freedom to Grow in a World of Opportunity

You will have the flexibility you need to do your best work with hybrid work options. Whether you’re working from an AECOM office, remote location or at a client site, you will be working in a dynamic environment where your integrity, entrepreneurial spirit and pioneering mindset are championed.

You will help us foster a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion – a safe and respectful workplace, where we invite everyone to bring their whole selves to work using their unique talents, backgrounds and expertise to create transformational outcomes for our clients.

AECOM provides a wide array of compensation and benefits programs to meet the diverse needs of our employees and their families. We also provide a robust global well-being program. We’re the world’s trusted global infrastructure firm, and we’re in this together – your growth and success are ours too.

Join us, and you’ll get all the benefits of being a part of a global, publicly traded firm – access to industry-leading technology and thinking and transformational work with big impact and work flexibility. As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in each person’s potential, and we’ll help you reach yours.

You Will Be Responsible For

About You

This is an opportunity to join a fast-growing organisation and play an integral part in its success and continued growth. To be successful in this role you will possess:

jobs.title: Environmental Health Safety Specialist
jobs.description:
Trinity Consultants is a global team of experts solving critical challenges in environmental compliance, ecological protection, infrastructure performance, and pharmaceutical development. From concept to execution, we provide the insight and innovation that help our clients succeed.

Trusted by over 10,000 clients worldwide, our team of 2,000+ experts bring deep specialization in engineering, science, chemistry, and sustainability. With local expertise across more than 100 offices, we understand regional regulations and deliver tailored solutions no matter the project.

Our staffing business line helps connect bright people with great companies. Our client in the automotive industry is seeking compliance support on a contract or direct hire basis. The position summary is representative.

Position Summary

The Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) Specialist is responsible for overseeing environmental compliance programs and supporting facility health and safety initiatives at a manufacturing operation in the Peru/LaSalle, Illinois area. This role serves as the site's primary environmental compliance resource, ensuring adherence to federal, state, and local environmental regulations while supporting the site's ISO 14001 Environmental Management System.

The successful candidate will have strong expertise in air permitting and compliance, wastewater and stormwater management, hazardous waste regulations, and environmental reporting. The position also provides leadership and support for occupational safety programs to maintain compliance with OSHA standards and drive continuous improvement in EHS performance.

Key Responsibilities

Environmental Compliance (Primary Focus)

Maintain and continuously improve the site's ISO 14001 Environmental Management System (EMS).
Serve as the facility environmental subject matter expert for compliance with:
Title V Air Permit requirements
NPDES permits
Industrial wastewater programs
Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPP)
Spill Prevention, Control and Countermeasure (SPCC) programs
Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) hazardous waste regulations
Manage environmental permits, inspections, monitoring, recordkeeping, and regulatory reporting.
Conduct environmental compliance audits and assessments to identify gaps and corrective actions.
Coordinate air emissions calculations, monitoring activities, and annual environmental reports.
Oversee hazardous waste management, storage, labeling, accumulation areas, and disposal activities.
Manage environmental contractors, laboratories, and waste disposal vendors.
Support regulatory agency inspections and maintain positive relationships with federal, state, and local regulators.
Investigate environmental incidents, spills, permit exceedances, or compliance concerns and implement corrective actions.
Track environmental performance metrics and communicate results to site leadership.

Health & Safety Responsibilities

Support site compliance with applicable OSHA regulations and company safety policies.
Conduct safety inspections, audits, and behavioral observations.
Assist with incident investigations, root cause analysis, and corrective action implementation.
Support programs involving:
Lockout/Tagout (LOTO)
Hazard Communication
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
Contractor Safety
Industrial Hygiene
Emergency Response
Develop and deliver EHS training programs for employees and contractors.
Participate in safety committees and promote a strong safety culture throughout the facility.

Leadership & Continuous Improvement

Lead environmental improvement projects that reduce risk, waste generation, emissions, and resource consumption.
Drive employee engagement through training, awareness campaigns, and environmental stewardship initiatives.
Maintain EHS documentation, procedures, records, and management system requirements.
Provide technical guidance to operations, maintenance, engineering, and leadership teams.
Support sustainability and corporate EHS initiatives as assigned.

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Industrial Technology, Occupational Safety, or another related technical discipline.
1 - 3 years of environmental compliance experience in a manufacturing, chemical, industrial, or process industry environment.
Demonstrated expertise with:
ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems
Title V Air Permitting and Compliance
NPDES Permitting
Wastewater Management
Stormwater Compliance Programs
SPCC Programs
Hazardous Waste Management and RCRA Regulations
Working knowledge of OSHA regulations and occupational safety programs.
Strong understanding of federal and Illinois environmental regulations.
Excellent organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and EHS recordkeeping systems.

Preferred

Environmental professional certification or safety certification (CHMM, CSP, CIH, REM, or equivalent).
Experience supporting chemical, metals, building products, food processing, or heavy manufacturing operations.
Experience managing environmental audits and regulatory inspections.
Knowledge of continuous improvement methodologies.

Key Competencies

Environmental Regulatory Expertise
ISO 14001 Management Systems
Environmental Auditing
Technical Problem Solving
Regulatory Reporting
Root Cause Analysis
Leadership and Employee Development
Communication and Collaboration
Risk Assessment
Continuous Improvement

Physical Requirements

Ability to work in both office and manufacturing environments.
Ability to conduct inspections throughout the facility, including climbing stairs and accessing production areas.
Ability to wear required PPE and occasionally work outdoors in varying weather conditions.

Target Candidate Profile

This position is ideal for an environmental professional with strong ISO 14001 and regulatory compliance experience who enjoys being the environmental leader for a manufacturing site while maintaining involvement in key health and safety initiatives. The successful candidate will be comfortable balancing regulatory compliance, employee engagement, auditing, training, and operational support in a fast-paced industrial environment.

jobs.company: The START Center for Cancer Research
jobs.title: Manager, Pharmacokinetic Lab
jobs.description:
The START Center for Cancer Research (“START”) is the world’s largest early phase site network, fully dedicated to oncology clinical research. Throughout our history, START has provided hope to cancer patients in global community practices by offering "Hope Through Access” to cutting edge trials throughout the United States and Europe.  

We are seeking a Manager, Pharmacokinetic Lab. This role will act as a liaison between START US Sites and the pharmaceutical sponsors by providing information regarding collection, processing, handling, storage, and shipment of research and clinical laboratory samples to ensure successful execution of the protocol within the SOPs of the department. Provides oversight for lab operations, facilities, SOPs, and quality metrics.

Work Schedule:  Monday-Friday 8:00am-5:00pm

Location: 4383 Medical Dr, San Antonio, TX 78229, United States

Essential Responsibilities

Oversee the processing of the samples by PK Lab Technicians and take appropriate corrective action to correct inconsistencies in collection data, as needed.
Create standard operating procedures (SOPs) for the PK Department and Tumor Bank and perform an annual review and / or update. Oversee or delegate training of PK Department staff on all PK Department SOPs, at least annually, when new SOPs are written, and when any updates occur.
Ensure compliance with all applicable Federal, State, and local laws and regulations as they apply to biological sample processing, handling, and shipping. Maintain accurate patient, study/protocol, and sponsor files.
Perform hiring, training, and development of employees. Supervise all personnel and new hires.
Oversee and complete study forms to include but not limited to: PK flowsheets, shipping logs, shipping documentation, sample requisition forms, flow sheets, and sample manifests.
Track Site Initiation Visits, protocol amendments and lab manual updates.
Participate in Protocol Development and Review Committee meetings by reviewing and providing comments for all phase 1 investigational protocols received by START.

Required Education And Experience

Bachelor’s degree in a chemical, physical, biological, or clinical laboratory science or medical technology.
At least five years laboratory setting experience.
Quality management skills including personnel management, financial management and process management.
Experience with electronic medical record program(s) and laboratory information systems.

Preferred Education And Experience

Prior experience in Phase I clinical trials.
Knowledge of GCP, GDPR and federal clinical research regulations required in US.
Experience in data management, logistics, and operations.

Best-in-Class Benefits and Perks 

We value the time, talent, and dedication our employees bring to START. Our commitment to your well-being and growth is reflected in a competitive compensation package—based on experience—along with comprehensive benefits designed to support you both personally and professionally: 

401(k) retirement savings plan with employer match 
Eligibility for an annual performance bonus, based on role and company results 
Generous paid time off and paid holidays 
Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage and optional insurance options 
Company p‑aid life and disability insurance for added financial protection 
Employee Assistance Program (EAP) providing confidential, no ‑cost support for you and your family from day one 
Flexible FSA and HSA plans to support your financial wellness 
Commitment to a supportive environment that values balance, wellbeing, and flexibility 
We’re committed to fostering a collaborative, creative workplace where every team member is encouraged to contribute. At START, you’ll join a team that values continuous learning, professional growth, shared ideas, and a culture built on inclusivity and innovation. 

More About START 

START clinical trial sites have conducted more than 1,000 early-phase clinical trials, including dozens of therapies that were approved by the FDA or EMA. START represents the world’s largest roster of early-phase principal investigators across its Network of clinical trial sites. Committed to accelerating passage from trials to treatments, START delivers hope to patients, families, and physicians around the world via our mission of “Hope Through Access”. As an example, in San Antonio, where START was founded, START treated the first patient ever with Keytruda – one of the most effective cancer drugs in medical history. 

Learn more at STARTresearch.com.  

Ready to be part of a team changing the future of cancer treatment? 

Join us in our mission to conquer cancer, one clinical trial at a time. Your expertise and dedication can help us bring hope and healing to patients worldwide. Please submit your application online. 

We are an equal opportunity employer that welcomes and encourages diversity in the workplace. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, marital status, age, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, pregnancy, genetic information, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other status protected under federal, state, or local law.

jobs.description:
ECS is seeking an experienced Senior Project Manager, with a clear path to Principal, to lead and grow our Environmental Compliance practice centered in Virginia, but expandable across the Mid-Atlantic. This role is built for a technically strong compliance professional who is equally energized by developing new business, mentoring a team, and shaping the future direction of our service offerings.

You will bring deep, hands-on expertise in air permitting, SPCC plans, and SWPPPs, and you will use that credibility to win new work, build client relationships, and expand what our compliance practice can offer. This is a role for someone ready to grow beyond individual project delivery into practice leadership, without losing touch with the technical work that got them here.

What You'll Own

Day-to-day leadership of environmental compliance projects, from scoping through delivery
Growth of the compliance service line; revenue, client base, and breadth of offerings
Mentorship and development of project managers, engineers, and field staff
A seat at the table in shaping practice strategy as you move toward a Principal role

Key Responsibilities:

Lead air permitting efforts, including Title V, NSR/PSD, and state minor-source permits, from application through agency negotiation
Prepare, implement, and audit Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure (SPCC) plans
Direct Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP) development, field inspections, and reporting
Serve as a technical resource on related programs; SPCC/FRP, RCRA, and multimedia compliance audits
Coordinate directly with state and federal regulators to resolve compliance issues and keep clients ahead of enforcement risk
Review technical reports, permits, and compliance documentation as appropriate
Identify and pursue new compliance work with existing and prospective clients
Build and maintain client relationships that lead to repeat and expanded engagements
Develop proposals, scopes, and fee estimates that win work and protect margins
Help identify and stand up new or adjacent service offerings for the compliance practice
Represent ECS at industry associations, agency meetings, and client events
Lead, mentor, and grow a team of compliance-focused project managers and staff
Provide oversight of project execution, quality, budgets, and schedules across the practice
Build internal training and career paths that strengthen bench depth for the practice
Collaborate with firm leadership to set goals and track performance for the compliance practice

Required Qualifications:

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, Geology, Chemical Engineering, or a related environmental discipline
7+ years of experience in environmental compliance, with direct experience in air permitting, SPCC, and SWPPP programs
Certified Hazardous Materials Manager (CHMM), Certified Environmental Professional (CEP), Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH), Certified Safety Professional (CSP), Professional Engineer (PE) license, Professional Geologist (PG) license or comparable professional certification preferred
Demonstrated experience managing client relationships and/or supporting business development
Prior experience mentoring or supervising junior staff
Strong technical foundation in air permitting, SPCC, and SWPPP compliance, with the judgment to lead complex, multi-site programs
Genuine interest in business development and strategic planning in addition to technical delivery
Track record of building and leading teams, with a mentoring mindset
Entrepreneurial outlook, with ideas for where the practice's service offerings could grow
Comfortable operating at both the technical, in-the-weeds level and the strategic, client-facing level

Military Qualifications

The following US Military ranks will qualify for this position IF they also meet the education and licenses requirements from the above section titled "Required Qualifications":
E-7

The expected pay range for this role and location is $80,000 - $120,000/year. The final agreed-upon compensation will be determined based on specific location and other individual qualifications.

We are employee-owned with more than 3,200 employees in 125 offices and testing facilities coast to coast. ECS is currently ranked #60 in Engineering News-Record’s Top 500 Design Firms (April 2026), #148 in Engineering News-Record’s Top 200 Environmental Firms (October 2025) and #38 in Zweig Group’s Hot Firm List (June 2026).

Location: Janesville, Wisconsin, United States (On-site)

We are seeking a dynamic Site EHS & HR Generalist to support daily safety initiatives and human resources functions within a fast-paced operational environment. This role serves as a trusted partner to employees and leaders, helping drive workplace safety, regulatory compliance, employee engagement, talent support, and organizational effectiveness.

Conduct workplace inspections, safety observations, audits, and risk assessments to identify and reduce potential hazards.

As we continue to expand, we're looking for high-performing professionals who are ready to lead, collaborate, innovate, and create impact. At Apex, you help shape what's next. All Apex positions are eligible for annual bonus opportunities, reinforcing our commitment to recognizing and rewarding meaningful contributions that drive our collective growth.

The Senior Technical Project Manager (PM) will lead and manage complex environmental investigation, remediation, and compliance projects involving chlorinated solvent impacts in soil, groundwater, sediment, soil vapor, and indoor air. The role requires strong technical leadership, client management, project delivery, staff development, and business development capabilities. Experience with large industrial, aerospace, manufacturing, military, and brownfield remediation programs is highly desirable.

Key Responsibilities

Project and Program Management

Manage large-scale environmental remediation projects from proposal through closure.
Develop project scopes, schedules, budgets, and health and safety plans.
Lead multidisciplinary teams of geologists, engineers, hydrogeologists, risk assessors, and environmental scientists.
Monitor project financial performance, including revenue, profitability, utilization, and forecasting.
Coordinate subcontractors, laboratories, drilling contractors, and remediation vendors.
Maintain quality assurance and quality control standards.

Technical Leadership

Serve as a technical lead for sites impacted by:
PCE (Tetrachloroethylene)
TCE (Trichloroethylene)
cis-1,2-DCE
Vinyl Chloride
Other chlorinated VOCs

Design and oversee:
Site investigations
Groundwater characterization
Soil vapor intrusion assessments
Human health and ecological risk assessments
Remedial investigations/feasibility studies (RI/FS)
Corrective action programs

Evaluate and implement remediation technologies such as:
In situ chemical reduction (ISCR)
In situ chemical oxidation (ISCO)
Enhanced reductive dechlorination (ERD)
Thermal remediation
Soil vapor extraction (SVE)
Dual-phase extraction (DPE)
Air sparging
Monitored natural attenuation (MNA)

Client Relationship Management

Act as primary client contact for key accounts.
Support strategic planning with industrial, aerospace, petroleum, manufacturing, and government clients.
Prepare and present technical findings to clients, regulators, and stakeholders.
Maintain long-term client relationships while identifying opportunities for additional services.

Business Development

Lead proposal preparation and pricing.
Support capture planning and opportunity pursuit.
Identify new clients and expand existing accounts.
Participate in industry organizations and conferences.

Regulatory Expertise

Demonstrated Experience Working With

EPA CERCLA/Superfund programs
RCRA Corrective Action
State cleanup programs
Vapor intrusion guidance
UST and industrial facility closure programs
California DTSC and Regional Water Board programs

Qualifications

BS in Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering, Geological Engineering, Hydrogeology, Geology, or related field.
12+ years of environmental consulting experience.
7+ years managing complex remediation projects.
Demonstrated success managing projects exceeding $500K to $5M+ annually.
Significant chlorinated solvent investigation and remediation experience.
California PE, PG, CHG, PMP, REM, CHMM (preferred)

Why You'll Love Working For Us

Company-subsidized medical and dental.
Company-paid life, short, and long-term disability.
401k match, tuition assistance, and more.
Cross-training and the ability to work on a variety of projects.
Performance-based bonuses or other incentives.
Working with the best and brightest in the industry.
2,000+ employee national firm with 70+ locations across the US.

new_jobs.description:
Company Description

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM’s Water Resources business is seeking an engaging and collaborative Sector Manager for our Victoria team.

Our Water Resources team delivers integrated, multidisciplinary services from flood risk and hydraulic modelling to drainage design, water quality and nature based solutions, across a range of projects including infrastructure, energy, defence, water utilities and airports.

This key leadership role will give you the opportunity to build networks across AECOM in Australia, New Zealand, and globally, from business operations through to management, while working closely with our leading specialists. Elevate your professional profile and carve a career pathway that truly makes a difference.

How you’ll make a difference

Guide the growth of the VIC Water Resources sector by fostering strong client partnerships, expanding market presence, diversifying our portfolio of services, and successfully delivering projects across the region.
Ensure technical and delivery excellence while maintaining the highest standards of quality, safety, governance, and client satisfaction.
Cultivate a collaborative, high-performing team culture by mentoring staff, providing technical direction, and nurturing growth.
Leverage regional and global expertise to drive innovation, implement best practices, and enhance delivery outcomes.

Qualifications

The following qualifications and experience are highly desired, but if you don’t tick all the boxes, you could still be a perfect fit for this role. Please apply, all applications will be considered.

The qualities that help you thrive

A relevant tertiary degree, CPEng, and ideally 20+ years of experience in water resources, including drainage, flooding, nature based solutions, water balance and yield assessments, and integrated water management.
A proactive, problem-solving mindset with the ability to champion innovative ideas, encourage initiative, and apply creative solutions.
A passion for leadership, mentoring, collaboration, and building strong relationships across diverse stakeholders.
Commercial and strategic acumen, with the ability to make informed decisions that balance profitability, efficiency, and market insight.

Additional Information

Why you’ll love working with us

Flexible work arrangements, including alternative start/finish times, part-time, job-sharing and hybrid work options
Purchase up to 6 weeks additional annual leave per year
Volunteer and representation leave
Flex public holidays – swap Easter or other holidays for ones that suit you better

Ready to push the limits of what’s possible?

We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, including those with disabilities, additional health or mental health needs, and/or neurodiverse conditions. If you require any adjustments during the hiring process, please let us know.

Applications are reviewed as they come in, and the role may close earlier than expected, so if this opportunity sounds like you, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

Learn more about life at AECOM:
LinkedIn, Facebook , Instagram, X, YouTube - explore our AECOM voices, employee stories, latest projects, and much more!

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

AECOM acknowledges the Traditional Owners and Custodians of the lands on which we, our clients and our communities live and work around Australia. We pay our respects to their cultures and to their Elders — past, present, and emerging. We are committed to connecting to Country in our work through meaningful engagement with First Nations peoples and businesses. Find out more about our Australian Reconciliation Action Plan here: https://aecom.com/au/our-vision-for-reconciliation/.

About AECOM

AECOM is the world’s trusted infrastructure consulting firm, delivering professional services throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. On projects spanning transportation, buildings, water, new energy and the environment, our public- and private-sector clients trust us to solve their most complex challenges. Our teams are driven by a common purpose to deliver a better world through our unrivaled technical and digital expertise, a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion, and a commitment to environmental, social and governance priorities. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm and its Professional Services business had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. See how we are delivering sustainable legacies for generations to come at aecom.com and @AECOM.

Freedom to Grow in a World of Opportunity

You will have the flexibility you need to do your best work with hybrid work options. Whether you’re working from an AECOM office, remote location or at a client site, you will be working in a dynamic environment where your integrity, entrepreneurial spirit and pioneering mindset are championed.

You will help us foster a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion – a safe and respectful workplace, where we invite everyone to bring their whole selves to work using their unique talents, backgrounds and expertise to create transformational outcomes for our clients.

AECOM provides a wide array of compensation and benefits programs to meet the diverse needs of our employees and their families. We also provide a robust global well-being program. We’re the world’s trusted global infrastructure firm, and we’re in this together – your growth and success are ours too.

Join us, and you’ll get all the benefits of being a part of a global, publicly traded firm – access to industry-leading technology and thinking and transformational work with big impact and work flexibility. As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in each person’s potential, and we’ll help you reach yours.

new_jobs.description:
Trinity Consultants is a global team of experts solving critical challenges in environmental compliance, ecological protection, infrastructure performance, and pharmaceutical development. From concept to execution, we provide the insight and innovation that help our clients succeed.

Trusted by over 10,000 clients worldwide, our team of 2,000+ experts bring deep specialization in engineering, science, chemistry, and sustainability. With local expertise across more than 100 offices, we understand regional regulations and deliver tailored solutions no matter the project.

Our staffing business line helps connect bright people with great companies. Our client in the automotive industry is seeking compliance support on a contract or direct hire basis. The position summary is representative.

Position Summary

The Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) Specialist is responsible for overseeing environmental compliance programs and supporting facility health and safety initiatives at a manufacturing operation in the Peru/LaSalle, Illinois area. This role serves as the site's primary environmental compliance resource, ensuring adherence to federal, state, and local environmental regulations while supporting the site's ISO 14001 Environmental Management System.

The successful candidate will have strong expertise in air permitting and compliance, wastewater and stormwater management, hazardous waste regulations, and environmental reporting. The position also provides leadership and support for occupational safety programs to maintain compliance with OSHA standards and drive continuous improvement in EHS performance.

Key Responsibilities

Environmental Compliance (Primary Focus)

Maintain and continuously improve the site's ISO 14001 Environmental Management System (EMS).
Serve as the facility environmental subject matter expert for compliance with:
Title V Air Permit requirements
NPDES permits
Industrial wastewater programs
Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPP)
Spill Prevention, Control and Countermeasure (SPCC) programs
Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) hazardous waste regulations
Manage environmental permits, inspections, monitoring, recordkeeping, and regulatory reporting.
Conduct environmental compliance audits and assessments to identify gaps and corrective actions.

The START Center for Cancer Research (“START”) is the world’s largest early phase site network, fully dedicated to oncology clinical research. Throughout our history, START has provided hope to cancer patients in global community practices by offering "Hope Through Access” to cutting edge trials throughout the United States and Europe.  

We are seeking a Manager, Pharmacokinetic Lab. This role will act as a liaison between START US Sites and the pharmaceutical sponsors by providing information regarding collection, processing, handling, storage, and shipment of research and clinical laboratory samples to ensure successful execution of the protocol within the SOPs of the department. Provides oversight for lab operations, facilities, SOPs, and quality metrics.

Work Schedule:  Monday-Friday 8:00am-5:00pm

Location: 4383 Medical Dr, San Antonio, TX 78229, United States

Essential Responsibilities

Oversee the processing of the samples by PK Lab Technicians and take appropriate corrective action to correct inconsistencies in collection data, as needed.
Create standard operating procedures (SOPs) for the PK Department and Tumor Bank and perform an annual review and / or update. Oversee or delegate training of PK Department staff on all PK Department SOPs, at least annually, when new SOPs are written, and when any updates occur.
Ensure compliance with all applicable Federal, State, and local laws and regulations as they apply to biological sample processing, handling, and shipping. Maintain accurate patient, study/protocol, and sponsor files.
Perform hiring, training, and development of employees. Supervise all personnel and new hires.
Oversee and complete study forms to include but not limited to: PK flowsheets, shipping logs, shipping documentation, sample requisition forms, flow sheets, and sample manifests.
Track Site Initiation Visits, protocol amendments and lab manual updates.
Participate in Protocol Development and Review Committee meetings by reviewing and providing comments for all phase 1 investigational protocols received by START.

Required Education And Experience

Bachelor’s degree in a chemical, physical, biological, or clinical laboratory science or medical technology.
At least five years laboratory setting experience.
Quality management skills including personnel management, financial management and process management.
Experience with electronic medical record program(s) and laboratory information systems.

Preferred Education And Experience

Prior experience in Phase I clinical trials.
Knowledge of GCP, GDPR and federal clinical research regulations required in US.
Experience in data management, logistics, and operations.

Employee Assistance Program (EAP) providing confidential, no ‑cost support for you and your family from day one

START clinical trial sites have conducted more than 1,000 early-phase clinical trials, including dozens of therapies that were approved by the FDA or EMA.
